sanskrit: rāghaveṇābhaye datte saṃnato rāvaṇānujaḥ khāt papātāvaniṃ hṛṣṭo bhaktair anucaraiḥ saha
english: When Rāghava had granted him safety, Rāvaṇa's younger brother bowed and, overjoyed, descended from the sky to the earth together with his devoted attendants.

sanskrit: sa tu rāmasya dharmātmā nipapāta vibhīṣaṇaḥ pādayoḥ śaraṇānveṣī caturbhiḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ
english: That righteous Vibhīṣaṇa, seeking refuge, fell at Rāma's feet together with four rākṣasas.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā rāmaṃ vākyaṃ tatra vibhīṣaṇaḥ dharmayuktaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca sāmprataṃ saṃpraharṣaṇam
english: There Vibhīṣaṇa then spoke these words to Rāma — words that were righteous, fitting, timely, and gladdening.

sanskrit: anujo rāvaṇasyāhaṃ tena cāsmy avamānitaḥ bhavantaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: "I am the younger brother of Rāvaṇa, and by him I have been dishonoured. I have come to you for refuge — you who are the refuge of all beings."

sanskrit: parityaktā mayā laṅkā mitrāṇi ca dhanāni ca bhavadgataṃ me rājyaṃ ca jīvitaṃ ca sukhāni ca
english: "I have abandoned Laṅkā, my friends, and my wealth. My kingdom, my life, and my pleasures are all now surrendered to you."

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ vadhe sāhyaṃ laṅkāyāś ca pradharṣaṇe kariṣyāmi yathāprāṇaṃ śaktiṃ pravekṣyāmi ca vāhinīm
english: "I will render assistance in the slaying of the rākṣasas and in the assault upon Laṅkā with all the strength of my life, and I will enter your army."

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇaṃ rāmas tu pariṣvajya vibhīṣaṇam abravīl lakṣmaṇaṃ prītaḥ samudrāj jalam ānaya
english: As he spoke thus, Rāma embraced Vibhīṣaṇa and, filled with joy, said to Lakṣmaṇa: "Bring water from the ocean."

sanskrit: tena cemaṃ mahāprājñam abhiṣiñca vibhīṣaṇam rājānaṃ rakṣasāṃ kṣipraṃ prasanne mayi mānada
english: "With it, quickly anoint this greatly wise Vibhīṣaṇa as king of the rākṣasas, O bestower of honour, now that I am pleased with him."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu saumitrir abhyaṣiñcad vibhīṣaṇam madhye vānaramukhyānāṃ rājānaṃ rāmaśāsanāt
english: Thus instructed, Saumitri anointed Vibhīṣaṇa as king in the midst of the foremost monkeys, acting on Rāma's command.

sanskrit: taṃ prasādaṃ tu rāmasya dṛṣṭvā sadyaḥ plavaṃgamāḥ pracukruśur mahānādān sādhu sādhv iti cābruvan
english: Witnessing that gracious act of Rāma, the monkeys at once raised great shouts and cried out, "Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: abravīc ca hanūmāṃś ca sugrīvaś ca vibhīṣaṇam kathaṃ sāgaram akṣobhyaṃ tarāma varuṇālayam
english: Then Hanūmān and Sugrīva asked Vibhīṣaṇa: "How shall we cross the impassable ocean, the abode of Varuṇa?"

sanskrit: upāyair abhigacchāmo yathā nadanadīpatim tarāma tarasā sarve sasainyā varuṇālayam
english: "Let us approach by means of some stratagem, so that we may all — together with the army — cross swiftly the lord of rivers and streams, the abode of Varuṇa."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dharmajñaḥ pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ samudraṃ rāghavo rājā śaraṇaṃ gantum arhati
english: Thus addressed, Vibhīṣaṇa, who knows what is right, replied: "King Rāghava ought to approach the ocean for refuge."

sanskrit: khānitaḥ sagareṇāyam aprameyo mahodadhiḥ kartum arhati rāmasya jñāteḥ kāryaṃ mahodadhiḥ
english: "This measureless great ocean was dug out by Sagara; the great ocean ought therefore to render service to Rāma, his kinsman."

sanskrit: evaṃ vibhīṣaṇenokte rākṣasena vipaścitā prakṛtyā dharmaśīlasya rāghavasyāpy arocata
english: When the wise rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa had spoken thus, this course also found favour with Rāghava, who was by nature righteous.

sanskrit: sa lakṣmaṇaṃ mahātejāḥ sugrīvaṃ ca harīśvaram satkriyārthaṃ kriyādakṣaḥ smitapūrvam uvāca ha
english: Then that great-spirited one, skilled in proper conduct and seeking to honour the occasion, spoke with a gentle smile to Lakṣmaṇa and to Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇasya mantro 'yaṃ mama lakṣmaṇa rocate brūhi tvaṃ sahasugrīvas tavāpi yadi rocate
english: "Lakṣmaṇa, this counsel of Vibhīṣaṇa pleases me. Speak, you together with Sugrīva — does it please you as well?"

sanskrit: sugrīvaḥ paṇḍito nityaṃ bhavān mantravicakṣaṇaḥ ubhābhyāṃ saṃpradhāryāryaṃ rocate yat tad ucyatām
english: "Sugrīva is ever wise, and you are expert in counsel; having considered the matter, both of you — say what seems best."

sanskrit: evam uktau tu tau vīrāv ubhau sugrīvalakṣmaṇau samudācāra saṃyuktam idaṃ vacanam ūcatuḥ
english: Thus addressed, those two heroes, Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa, both spoke this reply, combined with proper courteous form.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ no naravyāghra na rociṣyati rāghava vibhīṣaṇena yat tūktam asmin kāle sukhāvaham
english: "Why would it not please us, O tiger among men, O Rāghava? What Vibhīṣaṇa has said is agreeable and suited to this moment."

sanskrit: abaddhvā sāgare setuṃ ghore 'smin varuṇālaye laṅkā nāsādituṃ śakyā sendrair api surāsuraiḥ
english: "Without building a bridge across this dreadful ocean, the abode of Varuṇa, Laṅkā cannot be reached even by the gods and asuras together with Indra."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇasya śūrasya yathārthaṃ kriyatāṃ vacaḥ alaṃ kālātyayaṃ kṛtvā samudro 'yaṃ niyujyatām
english: "Let the true word of the valiant Vibhīṣaṇa be carried out. Enough delay — let this ocean now be made to serve."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ kuśāstīrṇe tīre nadanadīpateḥ saṃviveśa tadā rāmo vedyām iva hutāśanaḥ
english: Thus counselled, Rāma then lay down upon the shore of the lord of rivers and streams, which was spread with kuśa grass, like fire resting on a sacrificial altar.

sanskrit: tasya rāmasya suptasya kuśāstīrṇe mahītale niyamād apramattasya niśās tisro 'ticakramuḥ
english: As Rāma lay there on the ground spread with kuśa grass, vigilant and self-restrained, three nights passed over him.

sanskrit: na ca darśayate mandas tadā rāmasya sāgaraḥ prayatenāpi rāmeṇa yathārham abhipūjitaḥ
english: Yet the sluggish ocean would not reveal itself to Rāma, even though Rāma had worshipped it with all due observance and effort.

sanskrit: samudrasya tataḥ kruddho rāmo raktāntalocanaḥ samīpastham uvācedaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣmaṇam
english: Then Rāma, enraged at the ocean, his eyes red at the corners, spoke thus to Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks, who stood nearby.

sanskrit: paśya tāvad anāryasya pūjyamānasya lakṣmaṇa avalepaṃ samudrasya na darśayati yat svayam
english: "Look, Lakṣmaṇa, at the arrogance of this ignoble ocean, which, though honoured, does not appear before me of its own accord."

sanskrit: praśamaś ca kṣamā caiva ārjavaṃ priyavāditā asāmarthyaṃ phalanty ete nirguṇeṣu satāṃ guṇāḥ
english: "Composure, forbearance, uprightness, gentle speech — these virtues of good men bear the fruit of powerlessness when directed at those who are without virtue."

sanskrit: ātmapraśaṃsinaṃ duṣṭaṃ dhṛṣṭaṃ viparidhāvakam sarvatrotsṛṣṭadaṇḍaṃ ca lokaḥ satkurute naram
english: "The world honours a man who praises himself, who is wicked, bold, reckless, and who wields the rod of punishment on all sides."

sanskrit: na sāmnā śakyate kīrtir na sāmnā śakyate yaśaḥ prāptuṃ lakṣmaṇa loke 'smiñ jayo vā raṇamūdhani
english: "By gentleness, Lakṣmaṇa, fame cannot be won; by gentleness, glory cannot be won in this world, nor victory on the field of battle."

sanskrit: adya madbāṇanirbhinnair makarair makarālayam niruddhatoyaṃ saumitre plavadbhiḥ paśya sarvataḥ
english: "Today, O Saumitri, look at the abode of the makaras with its waters blocked and its makaras pierced by my arrows, floating on all sides."

sanskrit: mahābhogāni matsyānāṃ kariṇāṃ ca karān iha bhogāṃś ca paśya nāgānāṃ mayā bhinnāni lakṣmaṇa
english: "Behold here, Lakṣmaṇa, the great fish, the trunks of elephants, and the coiled bodies of serpents, all pierced by me."

sanskrit: saśaṅkhaśuktikā jālaṃ samīnamakaraṃ śaraiḥ adya yuddhena mahatā samudraṃ pariśoṣaye
english: "Today, with great battle, I shall dry up with my arrows the ocean together with its conches, oysters, fish, and makaras."

sanskrit: kṣamayā hi samāyuktaṃ mām ayaṃ makarālayaḥ asamarthaṃ vijānāti dhik kṣamām īdṛśe jane
english: "This abode of makaras takes me, endowed with forbearance, to be powerless. Fie upon forbearance toward such a person!"

sanskrit: cāpam ānaya saumitre śarāṃś cāśīviṣopamān adyākṣobhyam api kruddhaḥ kṣobhayiṣyāmi sāgaram
english: "Bring my bow, O Saumitri, and arrows like venomous serpents. Today, in my fury, I shall agitate even the impassable ocean."

sanskrit: velāsu kṛtamaryādaṃ sahasormisamākulam nirmaryādaṃ kariṣyāmi sāyakair varuṇālayam
english: "With my arrows I shall render boundless this abode of Varuṇa, which abides within its shores, suddenly churning with waves."

sanskrit: evam uktvā dhanuṣpāṇiḥ krodhavisphāritekṣaṇaḥ babhūva rāmo durdharṣo yugāntāgnir iva jvalan
english: Having spoken thus, with bow in hand and eyes dilated with rage, Rāma became terrible, blazing like the fire at the end of an age.

sanskrit: saṃpīḍya ca dhanur ghoraṃ kampayitvā śarair jagat mumoca viśikhān ugrān vajrāṇīva śatakratuḥ
english: Straining that dreadful bow and shaking the world with his arrows, he released fierce shafts like Śatakratu hurling thunderbolts.

sanskrit: te jvalanto mahāvegās tejasā sāyakottamāḥ praviśanti samudrasya salilaṃ trastapannagam
english: Those blazing, swiftly flying, supremely powerful arrows entered the waters of the ocean, terrifying the serpents therein.

sanskrit: tato vegaḥ samudrasya sanakramakaro mahān saṃbabhūva mahāghoraḥ samārutaravas tadā
english: Then a great and terrible agitation arose in the ocean, filled with crocodiles and makaras, accompanied by a roar like that of a tempest.

sanskrit: mahormimālāvitataḥ śaṅkhaśuktisamākulaḥ sadhūmaparivṛttormiḥ sahasābhūn mahodadhiḥ
english: The great ocean, spread with garlands of mighty waves, teeming with conches and oysters, its waves suddenly wreathed in smoke, was thrown into turmoil.

sanskrit: vyathitāḥ pannagāś cāsan dīptāsyā dīptalocanāḥ dānavāś ca mahāvīryāḥ pātālatalavāsinaḥ
english: The serpents were afflicted, their mouths and eyes blazing; and the dānavas of great might who dwell in the depths of Pātāla were terrified.

sanskrit: ūrmayaḥ sindhurājasya sanakramakarās tadā vindhyamandarasaṃkāśāḥ samutpetuḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: The waves of the lord of rivers, teeming with crocodiles and makaras, rose up by the thousands, resembling the Vindhya and Mandara mountains.

sanskrit: āghūrṇitataraṅgaughaḥ saṃbhrāntoragarākṣasaḥ udvartita mahāgrāhaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ salilāśayaḥ
english: With its mass of waves churning turbulently, its serpents and rākṣasas thrown into confusion, its great sea-monsters surging upward, the ocean was overwhelmed.

sanskrit: tato madhyāt samudrasya sāgaraḥ svayam utthitaḥ udayan hi mahāśailān meror iva divākaraḥ pannagaiḥ saha dīptāsyaiḥ samudraḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: Then the ocean rose of its own accord from its midst; the ocean appeared, ascending like the sun rising over the great mountains of Meru, accompanied by serpents with blazing mouths.

sanskrit: snigdhavaidūryasaṃkāśo jāmbūnadavibhūṣitaḥ raktamālyāmbaradharaḥ padmapatranibhekṣaṇaḥ
english: He had the glossy hue of vaidūrya gem, adorned with jāmbūnada gold, wearing a red garland and garments, his eyes resembling lotus petals.

sanskrit: sāgaraḥ samatikramya pūrvam āmantrya vīryavān abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ rāghavaṃ śarapāṇinam
english: The mighty ocean, having emerged and first paying homage, spoke with joined palms to Rāghava, who stood with arrow in hand.

sanskrit: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca rāghavaḥ svabhāve saumya tiṣṭhanti śāśvataṃ mārgam āśritāḥ
english: "O Rāghava, earth, wind, sky, water, and fire abide, O gentle one, in their own nature, following the eternal path."

sanskrit: tat svabhāvo mamāpy eṣa yad agādho 'ham aplavaḥ vikāras tu bhaved rādha etat te pravadāmy aham
english: "This is my own nature too — that I am unfathomable and unfordable. But there could be a transformation, O Rādhā — this I declare to you."

sanskrit: na kāmān na ca lobhād vā na bhayāt pārthivātmaja grāhanakrākulajalaṃ stambhayeyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: "Neither out of desire, nor out of greed, nor out of fear, O son of a king, can I in any way restrain my waters, which are troubled by crocodiles."

sanskrit: vidhāsye rāma yenāpi viṣahiṣye hy ahaṃ tathā grāhā na prahariṣyanti yāvat senā tariṣyati
english: "I shall make provision, O Rāma, for that by which I can bear it; the crocodiles shall not attack for as long as the army is crossing."

sanskrit: ayaṃ saumya nalo nāma tanujo viśvakarmaṇaḥ pitrā dattavaraḥ śrīmān pratimo viśvakarmaṇaḥ
english: "This one, O gentle lord, is named Nala, the son of Viśvakarman; the illustrious one was granted a boon by his father and is equal to Viśvakarman."

sanskrit: eṣa setuṃ mahotsāhaḥ karotu mayi vānaraḥ tam ahaṃ dhārayiṣyāmi tathā hy eṣa yathā pitā
english: "Let this monkey of great energy build a bridge upon me; I shall support it, for he is like his father."

sanskrit: evam uktvodadhir naṣṭaḥ samutthāya nalas tataḥ abravīd vānaraśreṣṭho vākyaṃ rāmaṃ mahābalaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the ocean vanished. Then Nala rose up and that foremost of monkeys, exceedingly mighty, spoke these words to Rāma.

sanskrit: ahaṃ setuṃ kariṣyāmi vistīrṇe varuṇālaye pituḥ sāmarthyam āsthāya tattvam āha mahodadhiḥ
english: "I shall build a bridge across the wide abode of Varuṇa, drawing upon the ability of my father. The great ocean has spoken the truth."

sanskrit: mama mātur varo datto mandare viśvakarmaṇā aurasas tasya putro 'haṃ sadṛśo viśvakarmaṇā
english: "A boon was granted to my mother at Mandara by Viśvakarman; I am his own son, equal to Viśvakarman."

sanskrit: na cāpy aham anukto vai prabrūyām ātmano guṇān kāmam adyaiva badhnantu setuṃ vānarapuṃgavāḥ
english: "Nor indeed would I have proclaimed my own virtues without being asked. Let the foremost monkeys build the bridge this very day if they so wish."

sanskrit: tato nisṛṣṭarāmeṇa sarvato hariyūthapāḥ abhipetur mahāraṇyaṃ hṛṣṭāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: Then, dispatched by Rāma, the leaders of the monkey troops rushed in all directions into the great forest with joy, by the hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: te nagān nagasaṃkāśāḥ śākhāmṛgagaṇarṣabhāḥ babhañjur vānarās tatra pracakarṣuś ca sāgaram
english: Those monkeys, themselves like mountains, foremost among the hosts of tree-dwelling creatures, broke off trees there and dragged them to the ocean.

sanskrit: te sālaiś cāśvakarṇaiś ca dhavair vaṃśaiś ca vānarāḥ kuṭajair arjunais tālais tikalais timiśair api
english: The monkeys brought sāla trees, aśvakarṇa trees, dhava trees, bamboos, kuṭaja, arjuna, tāla, tikala, and timiśa trees.

sanskrit: bilvakaiḥ saptaparṇaiś ca karṇikāraiś ca puṣpitaiḥ cūtaiś cāśokavṛkṣaiś ca sāgaraṃ samapūrayan
english: With bilva, saptaparṇa, and flowering karṇikāra trees, with mango and aśoka trees, they filled the ocean.

sanskrit: samūlāṃś ca vimūlāṃś ca pādapān harisattamāḥ indraketūn ivodyamya prajahrur harayas tarūn
english: Those foremost monkeys, lifting trees both with roots and without roots like Indra's banners raised on high, carried and hurled them.

sanskrit: prakṣipyamāṇair acalaiḥ sahasā jalam uddhatam samutpatitam ākāśam apāsarpat tatas tataḥ
english: As mountains were hurled in, the water suddenly thrown upward leapt into the sky and scattered in all directions.

sanskrit: daśayojanavistīrṇaṃ śatayojanam āyatam nalaś cakre mahāsetuṃ madhye nadanadīpateḥ
english: Nala built the great bridge in the midst of the lord of rivers and streams — ten yojanas in breadth and a hundred yojanas in length.

sanskrit: śilānāṃ kṣipyamāṇānāṃ śailānāṃ tatra pātyatām babhūva tumulaḥ śabdas tadā tasmin mahodadhau
english: As rocks were thrown and mountains were cast down there upon that great ocean, a tumultuous sound arose.

sanskrit: sa nalena kṛtaḥ setuḥ sāgare makarālaye śuśubhe subhagaḥ śrīmān svātīpatha ivāmbare
english: That bridge built by Nala over the ocean, the abode of makaras, beautiful and glorious, shone like the path of Svāti in the sky.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
english: Then the gods together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the foremost seers —

sanskrit: āplavantaḥ plavantaś ca garjantaś ca plavaṃgamāḥ tam acintyam asahyaṃ ca adbhutaṃ lomaharṣaṇam dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni sāgare setubandhanam
english: — and all living beings beheld the bridging of the ocean, which was inconceivable, unbearable to look upon, wondrous, and hair-raising, while the monkeys leapt, swam, and roared.

sanskrit: tāni koṭisahasrāṇi vānarāṇāṃ mahaujasām badhnantaḥ sāgare setuṃ jagmuḥ pāraṃ mahodadheḥ
english: Those thousands of crores of mighty monkeys, building the bridge across the ocean, crossed to the further shore of the great sea.

sanskrit: viśālaḥ sukṛtaḥ śrīmān subhūmiḥ susamāhitaḥ aśobhata mahāsetuḥ sīmanta iva sāgare
english: That great bridge — wide, well-built, glorious, with level ground, firmly laid — shone in the ocean like a parting line in hair.

sanskrit: tataḥ pare samudrasya gadāpāṇir vibhīṣaṇaḥ pareṣām abhighatārtham atiṣṭhat sacivaiḥ saha
english: Then, on the further shore of the ocean, Vibhīṣaṇa with mace in hand stood with his ministers, ready to ward off attacks from enemies.

sanskrit: agratas tasya sainyasya śrīmān rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ jagāma dhanvī dharmātmā sugrīveṇa samanvitaḥ
english: At the head of that army, the illustrious Rāma, righteous of soul, bearing his bow, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva, advanced.

sanskrit: anye madhyena gacchanti pārśvato 'nye plavaṃgamāḥ salile prapatanty anye mārgam anye na lebhire ke cid vaihāyasa gatāḥ suparṇā iva pupluvuḥ
english: Others went by the middle, others of the monkeys by the flanks; some fell into the water, others could not find the path; some, taking to the sky, leapt like garuḍas.

sanskrit: ghoṣeṇa mahatā ghoṣaṃ sāgarasya samucchritam bhīmam antardadhe bhīmā tarantī harivāhinī
english: With its great roar, the terrible monkey army, as it crossed, drowned out the uplifted, terrible sound of the ocean.

sanskrit: vānarāṇāṃ hi sā tīrṇā vāhinī nala setunā tīre niviviśe rājñā bahumūlaphalodake
english: That army of monkeys, having crossed by Nala's bridge, encamped at the far shore at the command of the king, in a place rich in roots and fruits.

sanskrit: tad adbhutaṃ rāghava karma duṣkaraṃ samīkṣya devāḥ saha siddhacāraṇaiḥ upetya rāmaṃ sahitā maharṣibhiḥ samabhyaṣiñcan suśubhair jalaiḥ pṛthak
english: Beholding that wondrous and difficult feat, the gods together with siddhas and cāraṇas came to Rāma accompanied by the great seers and each separately anointed him with beautiful waters.

sanskrit: jayasva śatrūn naradeva medinīṃ sasāgarāṃ pālaya śāśvatīḥ samāḥ itīva rāmaṃ naradevasatkṛtaṃ śubhair vacobhir vividhair apūjayan
english: "Conquer your enemies, O king of men; protect the earth with its ocean for eternal ages" — with such auspicious and varied words they honoured Rāma, who was thus celebrated as a king of men.
